assessments.reasoning: The pinned ASF publisher plaintext returned at the cutoff matches the claim's full-source digest. Bytes [4955,5439) contain the preamble, 4(a), and all of 4(b). Their reported SHA-256 matches ee52409f453334a254db0ad763c0678995506f121b04ec4dfc885633c0ea09d3. The mandatory language directly establishes the file-level notice, prominence, and attribution requirements in the tested distribution.

challenge.method: Tested a distributed Source-form Derivative Work containing one file changed by the licensee and one distributed unchanged. Compared a prominent notice on the changed file identifying the licensee as having changed it with a generic package note leaving that file unmarked. Tested a local-only edit and Object-only delivery as boundaries.
challenge.results: The prominent file notice communicates the required attribution. A statement merely reporting that changes occurred omits who made them, and a generic package note leaving the file unmarked fails the requirement that the modified file carry the notice. The licensee's unchanged file creates no new duty under this assertion to attribute a change to the licensee. A local-only edit lacks the stipulated distribution. Object-only delivery falls outside the Source-specific claim. Section 4(b) itself contains no express Source-only limitation. Neither 4(d) nor the closing paragraph supplies a substitute for the modified-file notice. No contradictory text was found.

limitations: The hypothetical stipulates a Derivative Work. Applying that classification, establishing who changed a file, and judging prominence in an actual distribution require facts about the works, modification history, and presentation.
Exact placement, wording, presentation, other modification histories, and binary-only treatment are outside the assertion.
reasoning: Section 4(b) requires “any modified files to carry prominent notices stating that You changed the files.” Section 1 defines “You” as the individual or Legal Entity exercising the licensed permissions. The claim therefore identifies the correct actor, the files that must carry the notice, and what the notice must communicate. Distributed derivative Source is within the preamble's scope. Section 1 requires the revisions or other modifications to a work based on the Work to represent, as a whole, an original work of authorship. It excludes works that remain separable or merely link or bind by name to the interfaces of the Work or its Derivative Works.
